intro: Say your name out loud. Say it slowly. Can you hear the pieces? Every word you say is made of small sounds. Your ears can find them. Your mouth can say them one at a time. That is where reading starts.

Letters are a code for those sounds. The letter m stands for /m/. Put letters in a row and they spell a word. Learn the code and the letters tell you what to say. Cat. Ship. Cape. Words you can read all by yourself.

In this unit you will hear the first sound, the last sound and the middle sound. You will rhyme and clap. You will blend sounds into words and take words apart. Then you will learn the letters, the vowels, the letter teams and the silent e. By the end, you will crack the code.
bigQuestion: How do the sounds you hear become words you can read?

timeline.t: Say a word slowly and hear the sounds inside it
Find the first sound: /b/ for ball, /d/ for dog
Find the last sound and the middle sound
Rhyme: cat, hat, bat. The ends match
Blend /s/ /u/ /n/ into sun, then take it apart
Change one sound: pin, pan, man
Learn that each letter has a name and a sound
Meet the five vowels and their short sounds
Read the letter teams sh, ch and th
Add a silent e: cap becomes cape
Read a whole line, left to right, all by yourself

words.d: one small piece of a word that you hear
when two words end with the same sound, like cat and hat
one beat in a word; apple has two
saying sounds together fast so they make a word
the big form of a letter, like B
one of the letters a, e, i, o, u
two letters that make one sound together, like sh
an e at the end of a word that makes no sound but changes the vowel

test.q: How many sounds are in the word sun?
test.why: Say it slowly: s... u... n. That is three sounds.

test.q: What is the first sound in fish?
test.why: The sound at the very start of fish is /f/.
Bed and red both end with -ed. Their ends sound the same.

test.q: How many claps does elephant get?
test.why: El-e-phant. Three beats, so three claps.
Say the sounds fast and close together. They make map.

test.q: Change the /c/ in cat to /b/. What word do you get?
test.why: Take off /c/ and put on /b/. C-at becomes b-at.

test.q: When you read a word, what do you use?
test.why: You read with sounds. Map is /m/ /a/ /p/, not em-ay-pee.

test.q: Which word has a vowel in the middle that says its short sound?
test.why: Pig is consonant, vowel, consonant. The i says /i/.

test.q: What sound do c and h make together in chip?
test.why: C and h are a team. Together they say /ch/.

test.q: What does the silent e do in cape?
choices: Makes the a say its name
test.why: The e is silent. It tells the a to say its name, ay.

write.prompt: Pick one word you can read now, like ship or cape. Tell how you read it. Say what sounds you hear, what letters you see, and how you put them together.
tips: Start with your word. Write it big.
Say the sounds you hear, first to last.
Tell about any letter team or silent e.
Say how you blended the sounds into the word.
Draw a picture of your word.
